newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Parts of space probe could hit earth - TV.
newsitem.headline: Parts of space probe could hit earth - TV.

text.p: Parts of a stricken Russian Mars space probe which ran into difficulties shortly after lift-off could fall to earth although most will burn up as it re-enters the atmosphere, Russian commercial television said on Sunday.

NTV said the rocket had four thermoelectric generators fuelled by radioactive plutonium. A nuclear scientist told Reuters the plutonium, highly carcinogenic, was stored in cannisters designed to withstand shock of re-entering the earth's atmosphere.

"Unburned bits of the station could hit the earth," an NTV commentator said. "To make matters worse the station has four thermoelectric generators fuelled by radioactive plutonium," he added. Space officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.
The nuclear scientist, who declined to be named, said the plutonium was highly dangerous but stressed it would be well sealed and said there was virtually no risk of leakage.

"This plutonium isotope is several hundred times more radioactive than the plutonium used for military purposes...If it is spread over the earth it is highly dangerous and leads to an established increase in cancer diseases," he said.
"But the substance used in satellites is enclosed in special cannisters designed to withstand the heat of entering the earth's atmosphere and even the shock of a fall on solid rock."
